# How this reference app was made

Generated from the original project's own archetype (r7's pinned snapshot):

    mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeCatalog=local \
        -DarchetypeGroupId=de.terrestris -DarchetypeArtifactId=shogun-core-webapp-archetype \
        -DarchetypeVersion=5.3.14-SNAPSHOT -DgroupId=de.example -DartifactId=shogunref \
        -Dversion=1.0 -Dpackage=de.example.shogunref -Dwebapp-name=shogunref

then patched. Nothing in shogun-core itself is changed; every behaviour the
hidden tests check is the library's.

The archetype is out of date with the library at this snapshot, so:

1. `pom.xml`: the dependency `de.terrestris:shogun-core` (the parent pom) is
   `shogun-core-main` (the jar).
2. Four generated classes had `{package}.x.Y;` instead of `import ...x.Y;` (an
   archetype template escape that no longer renders); fixed to imports.
3. `ProjectContentInitializer` and `ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator` used a
   `LOG` field the library no longer has; each now declares its own logger.

For r8:

4. PostgreSQL instead of H2 (Rust has no H2 driver): the
   `org.postgresql:postgresql` 42.4.3 dependency (the version the parent pom
   manages), `hikari.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource`,
   `hibernate.dialect=de.terrestris.shoguncore.hibernate.ShogunPostgresqlDialect`
   (the library's own), and `jdbc.url`/`username`/`password` from `R8_JDBC_URL`,
   `R8_DB_USER`, `R8_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults: the sandbox's `aidb`, user `ai`).
5. REST security: the archetype's "demo scenario" lets ROLE_USER reach only
   `/rest/users` and keeps everything else for ROLE_ADMIN. For the slice
   (users, groups, roles, layers, layerdatasources, layerappearances) every
   user may call the endpoints and the library's entity permission evaluators
   decide, so permissions are exercised on every entity type of the slice.
6. Hibernate's second-level cache off: the Spring context set a cache region
   factory but never passed `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache`, so
   Hibernate's default (on) applied and entities were served from memory after
   the hidden tests had reset the database with SQL. Caching is not part of
   the contract (a port has none); with it off, every request reads the
   database.

Run (Java 8, port 8081):

    R8_JDBC_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db mvn -DskipTests jetty:run   (add -o once its dependencies are local)

`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create`: every start drops and recreates the schema
and the archetype's initial content (users admin/shogun and user/shogun,
roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER, two groups, two OSM layers).

# How this reference app was made

Generated from the original project's own archetype (r7's pinned snapshot):

    mvn archetype:generate -DarchetypeCatalog=local \
        -DarchetypeGroupId=de.terrestris -DarchetypeArtifactId=shogun-core-webapp-archetype \
        -DarchetypeVersion=5.3.14-SNAPSHOT -DgroupId=de.example -DartifactId=shogunref \
        -Dversion=1.0 -Dpackage=de.example.shogunref -Dwebapp-name=shogunref

then patched. Nothing in shogun-core itself is changed; every behaviour the
hidden tests check is the library's.

The archetype is out of date with the library at this snapshot, so:

1. `pom.xml`: the dependency `de.terrestris:shogun-core` (the parent pom) is
   `shogun-core-main` (the jar).
2. Four generated classes had `{package}.x.Y;` instead of `import ...x.Y;` (an
   archetype template escape that no longer renders); fixed to imports.
3. `ProjectContentInitializer` and `ProjectApplicationPermissionEvaluator` used a
   `LOG` field the library no longer has; each now declares its own logger.

For r8:

4. PostgreSQL instead of H2 (Rust has no H2 driver): the
   `org.postgresql:postgresql` 42.4.3 dependency (the version the parent pom
   manages), `hikari.dataSourceClassName=org.postgresql.ds.PGSimpleDataSource`,
   `hibernate.dialect=de.terrestris.shoguncore.hibernate.ShogunPostgresqlDialect`
   (the library's own), and `jdbc.url`/`username`/`password` from `R8_JDBC_URL`,
   `R8_DB_USER`, `R8_DB_PASSWORD` (defaults: the sandbox's `aidb`, user `ai`).
5. REST security: the archetype's "demo scenario" lets ROLE_USER reach only
   `/rest/users` and keeps everything else for ROLE_ADMIN. For the slice
   (users, groups, roles, layers, layerdatasources, layerappearances) every
   user may call the endpoints and the library's entity permission evaluators
   decide, so permissions are exercised on every entity type of the slice.
6. Hibernate's second-level cache off: the Spring context set a cache region
   factory but never passed `hibernate.cache.use_second_level_cache`, so
   Hibernate's default (on) applied and entities were served from memory after
   the hidden tests had reset the database with SQL. Caching is not part of
   the contract (a port has none); with it off, every request reads the
   database.

Run (Java 8, port 8081):

    R8_JDBC_URL=jdbc:postgresql://host:5432/db mvn -DskipTests jetty:run   (add -o once its dependencies are local)

`hibernate.hbm2ddl.auto=create`: every start drops and recreates the schema
and the archetype's initial content (users admin/shogun and user/shogun,
roles ROLE_ADMIN and ROLE_USER, two groups, two OSM layers).

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<beans:beans xmlns="http://www.springframework.org/schema/security"
       xmlns:beans="http://www.springframework.org/schema/beans"

    <!-- Authentication Manager -->
    <authentication-manager alias="authenticationManager">
        <authentication-provider ref="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" />
    </authentication-manager>
    <beans:bean id="basicAuthEntryPoint" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationEntryPoint">
        <beans:property name="realmName" value="SHOGun Realm" />
    </beans:bean>
    <beans:bean id="basicAuthenticationFilter" class="org.springframework.security.web.authentication.www.BasicAuthenticationFilter">
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="authenticationManager"/>
        <beans:constructor-arg ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" />
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- (Additional) Basic auth security for REST -->
    <http auto-config='false' entry-point-ref="basicAuthEntryPoint" pattern="/rest/**" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <!-- Demo scenario: users will only get access to the /rest/users interface -->
        <!-- r8: the slice is open to every user; entity permissions decide -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/users" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/groups" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/roles" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layers" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerdatasources" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <intercept-url pattern="/rest/layerappearances" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')"/>
        <!-- All other interfaces can only be accessed by admins -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.superAdminRoleName}')"/>
        <custom-filter ref="basicAuthenticationFilter" before="FORM_LOGIN_FILTER"/>
        <csrf disabled="true"/>
    </http>
    <!-- Web/URL security -->
    <http auto-config="true" use-expressions="true" access-decision-manager-ref="accessDecisionManager">
        <logout logout-url="/logout" />
        <!-- As CSRF protection is enabled by default in Spring Security 4,
             the logout-url will only work with POST requests. To work with
             GET requests CSRF has to be disabled -->
        <csrf disabled="false"/>
        <!-- URL security -->
        <intercept-url pattern="/login/**" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/register.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/activate.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/resetPassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/user/changePassword.action" access="permitAll" />
        <intercept-url pattern="/**" access="hasRole('${role.defaultUserRoleName}')" />
    </http>
    <!-- Enables Method Security and Expression-based access control -->
    <global-method-security pre-post-annotations="enabled">
        <!-- Enables custom expression handler -->
        <expression-handler ref="methodExpressionHandler" />
    </global-method-security>
    <!-- BEANS -->
    <!-- bcrypt password encoder -->
    <beans:bean id="bcryptEncoder" class="org.springframework.security.crypto.bcrypt.BCryptPasswordEncoder">
        <!-- Configure the strength (log rounds). Default = 10 -->
        <beans:constructor-arg value="10"/>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- Custom Authentication Provider -->
    <beans:bean id="shogunCoreAuthenticationProvider" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.ShogunCoreAuthenticationProvider">
        <beans:property name="passwordEncoder" ref="bcryptEncoder" />
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- This bean is referenced by the http security config to assure that the role hierarchy will be used -->
    <beans:bean id="accessDecisionManager" class="org.springframework.security.access.vote.AffirmativeBased">
        <beans:constructor-arg>
            <beans:bean id="webExpressionVoter" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.WebExpressionVoter">
                <beans:property name = "expressionHandler">
                    <beans:bean id="webExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.web.access.expression.DefaultWebSecurityExpressionHandler">
                        <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy" />
                    </beans:bean>
                </beans:property>
            </beans:bean>
        </beans:constructor-arg>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- See http://goo.gl/o42k1S -->
    <beans:bean id="methodExpressionHandler" class="org.springframework.security.access.expression.method.DefaultMethodSecurityExpressionHandler">
    <!-- To use hasPermission() in expressions, configure a PermissionEvaluator -->
         <beans:property name = "permissionEvaluator" ref="permissionEvaluator" />
         <beans:property name = "roleHierarchy" ref="roleHierarchy"/>
    </beans:bean>
    <beans:bean id="permissionEvaluator" class="de.terrestris.shoguncore.security.access.ShogunCorePermissionEvaluator">
        <beans:property name="permissionEvaluatorFactory">
            <!-- This is how project specific permission evaluators can be used/configured -->
            <beans:bean class="de.example.shogunref.security.access.factory.ProjectEntityPermissionEvaluatorFactory" />
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>
    <!-- http://static.springsource.org/spring-security/site/docs/3.0.x/apidocs/org/springframework/security/access/hierarchicalroles/RoleHierarchyImpl.html -->
    <beans:bean id="roleHierarchy"  class="org.springframework.security.access.hierarchicalroles.RoleHierarchyImpl">
        <beans:property name="hierarchy">
            <beans:value>
                ${role.superAdminRoleName} > ${role.defaultUserRoleName}
            </beans:value>
        </beans:property>
    </beans:bean>
</beans:beans>

content.text: The original uses OpenSessionInView, so one Hibernate session spans each request. That matters for PUT behaviour. Next I'll snapshot the seeded reference database so I can reset it between experiments.

cat > /tmp/harness/ref.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# usage: req BASE METHOD PATH [USER:PASS] [BODY]
req() {
  local base="$1" method="$2" path="$3" cred="$4" body="$5"
  local args=(-s -X "$method" -w '  [%{http_code}]\n' "$base$path")
  [ -n "$cred" ] && args+=(-u "$cred")
  if [ -n "$body" ]; then args+=(-H 'Content-Type: application/json' --data-binary "$body"); fi
  curl "${args[@]}"
}
reset_ref() { pg_restore --clean --if-exists --no-owner -d ref /tmp/ref_seed.dump >/dev/null 2>&1; }
export -f req reset_ref

content.text: Important discoveries. Bare JSON objects that are equal under Java `equals`, because they share a creation timestamp and content, collapse in sets, so `members: [{id:3},{id:4}]` keeps only user 3. Also, responses show in-memory state, not reloaded rows. I'll verify the role-dedup theory and then test DELETE behaviour.

---
name: shogun-rest-port-behaviour
description: Non-obvious behaviour of the Java SHOGun-Core REST slice that the Rust port in /work/rust must reproduce (status codes, output:only, id order, nulls, layer delete rule)
metadata:
  type: project
---

Rust port of /rest/{users,groups,roles,layers,layerdatasources,layerappearances} in /work/rust, checked
differentially against the Java reference app (port 8081, DB `ref`) with /tmp/harness/diff.py and
/tmp/harness/scenarios.py (DB `port` on port 9090). Reference DB seed dump: /tmp/ref_seed.dump.

Non-obvious facts found by running the original:
- Login: wrong pw / inactive / no authority at all -> 401; authenticated but no ROLE_USER -> 403.
  Roles = user roles + roles of its groups. ROLE_ADMIN implies ROLE_USER.
- Writes: POST -> 400 on any failure, including non-admin (CREATE is admin-only). PUT/DELETE -> 404 on any failure
  (denied, missing, FK, NOT NULL, unknown property). PUT needs body id == path id (else 400, missing id 400).
- output:only builds bare objects (constructor defaults, not DB values): non-admin gets [] for users/groups/layers,
  layerdatasources with output:only -> 500 (abstract class). Admin sees id null unless id requested.
- Filters only on the entity's own scalar fields (not subclass fields); unknown keys ignored; no valid key -> [].
  Bad int/bool/double values cast to 0/false/0.0 (BeanUtils ConvertUtils), so id=abc matches nothing.
- Bare JSON objects in a Set collapse when equal ignoring id: members [{id:3},{id:4}] keep only 3;
  roles [{id:1},{id:2}] keep only 1. Named objects are distinct.
- Responses show in-memory state: nested objects given in the body are echoed as sent (nulls for missing fields).
- Null collections stay null (userGroups:null -> null, not []).
- userGroups ids are resolved with READ (loadById); unknown id fails at body parse (no id consumed on POST);
  unreadable group fails at flush (id consumed on POST).
- ids: Hibernate generates the parent id before cascading to a new child (layer id 42, appearance 43).
  Failed inserts still consume ids (allocation is outside the request transaction).
- Layer DELETE by non-admin: needs READ (ok) and UPDATE on every map that lists the layer (LayerService.delete
  saves the map). Seed map 28 lists layers 15 and 16. Admin deletes remove the layer from maps_layers.
- Nested cascades: layer.appearance and tileGrid/extent are cascaded (SAVE_UPDATE); with an id that is already loaded
  in the request -> error (NonUniqueObject). layer.source and XYZ extent are not cascaded; abstract source JSON -> error.
- Permission collections are never deleted, only the join rows (userpermissions / grouppermissions).

**Why:** the hidden tests compare the port with the original on these exact paths.
**How to apply:** when changing handlers, rerun the differential harness (143+ scenarios) before trusting a change.

# shogun-rest

Rust port of the REST slice of SHOGun-Core (`/rest/users`, `/rest/groups`,
`/rest/roles`, `/rest/layers`, `/rest/layerdatasources`,
`/rest/layerappearances`) on the unchanged `schema.sql` database.

    cargo build --release --locked
    DATABASE_URL=postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db PORT=8080 target/release/shogun-rest

Layout:

- `src/http.rs` – HTTP Basic login (bcrypt, active flag, roles of the user and its groups),
  routing of the REST paths, status codes of unknown paths.
- `src/resources.rs` – the endpoints: list, filter, get, create, update (partial), delete,
  `output:only`, `users/{id}/userGroups`, `groups/{id}/users`, with READ/UPDATE/DELETE/CREATE rules.
- `src/perms.rs` – entity permission evaluation (user and group permission collections, ADMIN,
  self and membership rules, stripped objects of `output:only`).
- `src/jin.rs` – request bodies read as the original's Jackson mapper does (unknown properties
  refused, ignored properties accepted, coercions, set semantics of JSON arrays).
- `src/jout.rs` – JSON of the entities (nulls, embedded objects, ids of user groups).
- `src/db.rs` – SQL: loading the object graph, saving with Hibernate's cascades, id allocation from
  `hibernate_sequences` (outside the request transaction), deletes in Hibernate's order.
- `src/tests.rs` – unit tests of the mapping rules (`cargo test --release --locked`; no database needed).

No data is created or altered in the schema; all state lives in the tables of `schema.sql`.

The Rust port is in `/work/rust` and matches the original on every scenario I tested: 154 differential scenarios, all passing, with the same status codes, normalised JSON, and database rows.

**Verification**
- `cargo build --release --locked` passes from a clean `target/`. It has no warnings.
- `cargo test --release --locked` passes (19 unit tests). It also passes with `DATABASE_URL` set. The unit tests don't need a database.
- The service starts with `DATABASE_URL` and `PORT`, binds `0.0.0.0`, and connects lazily, so it answers at once.
- I ran the original on port 8081 and the port on 9090, each on its own copy of the same seed data. For each scenario I compared status codes, JSON, and the rows of about 28 affected tables (timestamps excluded).
- The scenarios cover login and roles, the six resources with GET, POST, PUT and DELETE, the nested user-group and group-member endpoints, permissions by user, group and ADMIN, `output:only`, filters, nested cascades, and the refused abstract data source.

**What's in the deliverable**
- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `README.md` and `src/` (about 3,700 lines). There is no `target/`.
- `http.rs` handles Basic auth, routing and HEAD. `resources.rs` has the endpoints and permission checks. `perms.rs` has the evaluator rules. `jin.rs` and `jout.rs` mirror the Jackson behaviour. `db.rs` has SQL, Hibernate-style saves and deletes, and id allocation.

**Behaviour I had to discover from the original**
- A non-admin can delete a layer only with UPDATE (or ADMIN) on every map that lists it. The seed map lists layers 15 and 16.
- `output:only` returns bare objects, so non-admins get `[]` for users, groups and layers, and a data-source `output:only` returns 500.
- Bare JSON objects collapse in sets. `members: [{id:3},{id:4}]` keeps only user 3.
- Ids are generated for the parent before its cascaded children. Failed inserts still consume ids.

**Known gaps**
- XYZ resolutions are written as Java-serialized Double bytes. I haven't checked that the original reads them back, and the spec doesn't require it.
- Timestamps and list order aren't compared, and JSON key order differs from Jackson. Error responses have empty bodies, not Jetty's HTML.
- The differential harness is in `/tmp/harness`, outside the deliverable. It needs the original running on 8081 and the reference seed dump.

I stopped the original and the port service at the end.

content.text:
The XYZ resolution writes are now compared with the original, and the port matches it. The full differential run passes 162 of 162 scenarios.

**What was wrong**
- Resolutions are a `List<Point2D.Double>`, not `List<Double>`: in `XyzLayerDataSource`, `Double` is imported from `java.awt.geom.Point2D`. The original therefore takes `{x, y}` objects, and it refuses bare numbers with 404. My port accepted numbers and stored bare doubles. It was also wrong for the inputs the original accepts.
- The original stores each point as Java-serialized `Point2D$Double` bytes. I took the constant class-descriptor prefix from bytes the original wrote, and the port writes the same prefix followed by x and y as big-endian doubles. A unit test checks the encoding byte for byte.
- Null elements behave the same way in four lists: tile-grid resolutions, WMTS URLs, WMTS matrix ids, and XYZ resolutions. The original keeps `null` in its response but skips it when storing. Resolution rows keep their list position as the index, so a gap in the index reloads as `null` in that position.

**Verification added**
- `xyz_*` scenarios: write, replace and clear, read as a user, numbers refused, null element, and a seeded row with a DB-written byte stream.
- `null_elements_in_lists`: tile-grid resolutions, WMTS URLs, and WMTS matrix ids.
- `seeded_index_gaps`: reloads rows with gaps in their indexes.
- A full run of all 162 scenarios passed afterwards. The compared database tables include `xyzlayerdatasrc_resolution`, `tilegrid_resolution`, `wmtslayerdatasources_urls` and `wmtstilegrids_matrixids`, so their bytes and rows are compared.
- `cargo build --release --locked` and `cargo test --release --locked` pass, with 19 unit tests.

**Still open**
- Timestamps and JSON key order are not compared. The XYZ byte stream was taken from the original's output, not from a published Java serializer, and I checked it only on point values from the original's own writes.

I removed `target/` and stopped the original and the port service.
